diagram_candidates.kind: two-flag intersection grid and Bruhat-position map
diagram_candidates.rationale: The theorem explicitly converts the intersection-dimension table of a pair of complete flags into the southwest rank matrix of h^{-1}g, then into a double coset and permutation. Its final remark itself refers to the direction of the picture, making a compact schematic particularly apt.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Draw two nested flags F_0<...<F_n and E_0<...<E_n with the n-by-n entries dim(F_i∩E_j). For the standard first flag and E=gV_•, annotate dim(V_i∩E_j)=j-r_{i+1,j}(g), where r_{i+1,j} is rank of g on rows i+1,...,n and columns 1,...,j; mark this southwest block to preserve the convention. Connect the grid to the southwest rank matrix, then to the unique permutation σ with Bruhat cell BP_σB and diagonal G-orbit. Do not imply the diagram proves the rank identity or orbit classification.
diagram_candidates.status: Optional but unusually well motivated by the item’s explicit picture remark; no proof depends on a diagram.

diagram_candidates.kind: colored KLR strand-generator and local-relation diagram
diagram_candidates.rationale: The definition gives idempotent words, dots, crossings, quadratic and braid relations, and geometric crossing classes. A small standard strand diagram can orient these indexed formulas and clarify which signs and color conditions accompany a crossing.
diagram_candidates.draw_or_check: Show m upward strands labelled by ν_1,...,ν_m, a dot x_r on strand r, and a crossing τ_r swapping adjacent colors. State τ_re_ν=e_{s_rν}τ_r; show distinct-color dot slides x_r↔x_{r+1}; for equal colors annotate the two mixed relations with +e_ν and −e_ν; show τ_r²e_ν=Q_{ν_rν_{r+1}}(x_r,x_{r+1})e_ν. For the braid relation, label the correction only in the outer-equal-color case ν_r=ν_{r+2} and write its polynomial quotient exactly as in lines 84–86. Include the signed geometric normalization in lines 65–72 only if the diagram distinguishes [C]standard from σ_r and τ_r.
diagram_candidates.status: Optional; useful as conventional KLR notation, but the exhaustive algebraic presentation is self-contained and no proof depends on a picture.
